description: This topic covers the meaning and importance of farm structures and buildings, their types, siting and construction factors, suitable building materials, requirements of a good livestock house, and maintenance practices on Tanzanian farms.

mcq.questionText: What is meant by the term 'farm structures'?

options.text: Only the crops grown on a farm
Permanent and semi-permanent constructions that support farming activities
The boundaries of a farmer's land only
The amount of money invested in a farm

mcq.explanation: Farm structures are the constructions such as buildings, stores, fences and water structures that are put up to support and improve farming activities.

mcq.questionText: Which farm building is used mainly to keep poultry?
mcq.explanation: A poultry house is specifically designed to provide shelter, protection and comfort for chickens and other birds.

mcq.questionText: Which structure is used for dipping cattle to control ticks and tick-borne diseases?
mcq.explanation: A cattle dip is a structure filled with acaricide solution through which cattle pass to kill ticks and control tick-borne diseases such as East Coast Fever.

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of a silo on a farm?

options.text: To store grain or silage for animal feed

mcq.explanation: A silo is a storage structure used to keep grain or to preserve fodder as silage for feeding livestock during the dry season.

mcq.questionText: Which factor is MOST important when choosing the wind direction for siting a livestock house?

options.text: The house should face into strong prevailing winds for cooling
The house should be placed so that bad smells are blown away from the farmhouse
Wind direction does not matter at all
The house must always face north regardless of wind

mcq.explanation: Buildings should be sited so that the prevailing wind carries smells and dust away from the home, keeping the homestead clean and healthy.

mcq.questionText: A structure used to restrain cattle so they can be treated, sprayed or examined is called a:
mcq.explanation: A crush is a narrow strong enclosure that holds an animal still so the farmer can spray, inject, dehorn or examine it safely.

mcq.questionText: Which building material is widely used for roofing farm buildings in Tanzania because it is durable and waterproof?
mcq.explanation: Corrugated iron sheets, known locally as mabati, are commonly used for roofing because they are strong, durable and keep out rain.

mcq.questionText: Why is good ventilation a requirement of a livestock house?

options.text: To increase the number of predators
To remove stale air, moisture and harmful gases such as ammonia
To make the building more expensive

mcq.explanation: Good ventilation provides fresh air and removes moisture, heat and gases like ammonia, which keeps animals healthy and comfortable.

mcq.questionText: What is a zero-grazing unit used for?

options.text: Keeping dairy cattle in one place where feed and water are brought to them
Allowing animals to roam freely over large pastures

mcq.explanation: In a zero-grazing unit, the dairy animals are confined in a shed and the feed, fodder and water are cut and carried to them, which suits areas with little grazing land.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a water structure on a farm?
mcq.explanation: Water structures include wells, water tanks and troughs that collect, store and supply water for crops and livestock.

mcq.questionText: Why should farm buildings be sited near a good road or path?

options.text: To make them more difficult to reach
For easy accessibility when moving inputs, produce and animals
To increase flooding around the building

mcq.explanation: Accessibility allows easy transport of feeds, produce, water and animals to and from the building, saving labour and time.

mcq.questionText: A greenhouse is mainly used to:

options.text: House cattle during the rainy season
Provide a controlled environment for growing crops such as tomatoes

mcq.explanation: A greenhouse creates a controlled environment of temperature and humidity that allows high-value crops like tomatoes and capsicum to be grown well, including in the off-season.

mcq.questionText: Which material is suitable for making strong, fire-resistant and long-lasting farm building walls?
mcq.explanation: Burnt bricks and cement blocks make strong, durable and fire-resistant walls, although they are more expensive than poles and mud.

mcq.questionText: What is the main reason for regular maintenance of farm structures?

options.text: To keep them in good working condition and prolong their life
To reduce the value of the farm

mcq.explanation: Regular maintenance such as repairing roofs and fences keeps structures functioning, prevents serious damage and extends their useful life.

mcq.questionText: Which structure provides living accommodation for the farmer and the family on a farm?
mcq.explanation: The farmhouse is the building where the farmer and family live; it is usually placed in a central, secure and well-drained part of the farm.

fib.questionText: A structure used to store harvested grain such as maize or sorghum is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A granary (ghala) is a store specially built to keep harvested grain dry and safe from pests.

fib.questionText: The narrow structure used to hold an animal still during spraying or injection is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A crush restrains animals so they can be treated, examined or sprayed safely.

fib.questionText: In a _____ unit, dairy cattle are kept in one place and feed is brought to them instead of grazing.
fib.explanation: Zero-grazing keeps animals confined and the farmer cuts and carries feed to them, which suits areas with limited land.

fib.questionText: Corrugated iron sheets used for roofing farm buildings are locally known in Tanzania as _____.
fib.explanation: Mabati is the Swahili word for corrugated iron sheets, which are durable and waterproof roofing materials.

fib.questionText: A good livestock house must have proper _____ to allow fresh air in and remove stale air and gases.
fib.explanation: Ventilation supplies fresh air and removes moisture, heat and harmful gases, keeping animals healthy.

fib.questionText: A structure filled with acaricide through which cattle pass to control ticks is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A cattle dip contains acaricide solution that kills ticks and helps control tick-borne diseases.

fib.questionText: A house specially built for keeping pigs is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A pig sty provides shelter, wallowing space and protection for pigs.

fib.questionText: Farm buildings should be sited on _____ ground to avoid water-logging and flooding.
fib.explanation: Good drainage keeps buildings dry, prevents flooding and reduces disease, so structures are placed on well-drained, slightly raised ground.

fib.questionText: The building where milk is collected from dairy cows under clean conditions is called a milking _____.
fib.explanation: A milking parlour is a clean, special building where dairy cows are milked hygienically.

fib.questionText: A storage structure used to preserve green fodder as silage for the dry season is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A silo preserves fodder as silage so livestock have feed during the dry season when pasture is scarce.

tf.questionText: Farm structures help to increase efficiency and protect crops, animals and inputs on a farm.
tf.explanation: Well-built structures protect animals, store produce and inputs safely, and make farm work more efficient.

tf.questionText: A poultry house and a pig sty are exactly the same type of building.
tf.explanation: A poultry house is designed for birds while a pig sty is designed for pigs; their designs and requirements differ.

tf.questionText: Livestock buildings should be sited downwind so that smells are blown away from the farmhouse.
tf.explanation: Placing animal houses downwind keeps bad smells and dust away from the home, improving hygiene and comfort.

tf.questionText: Grass thatch is more durable and fire-resistant than corrugated iron sheets.
tf.explanation: Grass thatch is cheap but it rots, leaks and burns easily, so it is less durable and far less fire-resistant than iron sheets.

tf.questionText: A good livestock house should be easy to clean to help control diseases and parasites.
tf.explanation: Easy cleaning removes dung and dirt that harbour disease organisms and parasites, keeping animals healthy.

tf.questionText: Overcrowding animals in a small house is good because it saves space and keeps them warm.
tf.explanation: Overcrowding causes stress, spread of disease and poor growth; a good house provides adequate space per animal.

tf.questionText: Wells, tanks and troughs are examples of water structures found on a farm.
tf.explanation: Wells supply water, tanks store it and troughs provide drinking water for livestock, so all are water structures.

tf.questionText: Maintenance of farm structures is unnecessary once they are built.
tf.explanation: Structures must be maintained regularly by repairing roofs, fences and walls to keep them safe and prolong their life.

tf.questionText: Fences and gates help to provide security and control the movement of animals on a farm.
tf.explanation: Fences mark boundaries, keep animals in or out and improve security, while gates allow controlled entry and exit.

tf.questionText: A greenhouse can be used to grow high-value vegetables under a controlled environment.
tf.explanation: Greenhouses control temperature, humidity and pests, allowing crops such as tomatoes and sweet pepper to be grown well even off-season.

summary.correctAnswer: Farm structures and buildings are the permanent and semi-permanent constructions, such as livestock houses, stores, fences and water structures, that are put up to support and improve farming activities.
summary.explanation: This captures both the constructions and their purpose of supporting farm work.

summary.questionText: State three importances of farm structures.
summary.correctAnswer: They protect animals and crops from weather and predators, provide safe storage for produce and inputs, and improve efficiency and security of farm operations.
summary.explanation: Farm structures protect, store and make work more efficient and secure.

summary.questionText: List four types of livestock housing.
summary.correctAnswer: Cattle sheds or zero-grazing units, poultry houses, pig sties, and goat or sheep houses.
summary.explanation: These are the main buildings used to shelter different kinds of livestock.

summary.questionText: Name four factors to consider when siting farm buildings.
summary.correctAnswer: Drainage, accessibility, wind direction, water supply, security, and distance from the home are all considered.
summary.explanation: Good siting ensures buildings are dry, reachable, secure and conveniently placed.

summary.questionText: List five common materials used for constructing farm buildings.
summary.correctAnswer: Bricks, timber, iron sheets (mabati), cement, poles, and grass.
summary.explanation: These materials are chosen according to cost, durability and the purpose of the structure.

summary.questionText: State four requirements of a good livestock house.
summary.correctAnswer: Good ventilation, adequate lighting, easy to clean, protection from weather and predators, and adequate space for the animals.
summary.explanation: A good house keeps animals healthy, comfortable and safe.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between a crush and a dip.
summary.correctAnswer: A crush is a narrow enclosure that restrains an animal for treatment or examination, while a dip is a structure filled with acaricide through which cattle pass to control ticks.
summary.explanation: A crush holds an animal still; a dip removes ticks using acaricide.

summary.questionText: Why is drainage an important factor when siting farm buildings?
summary.correctAnswer: Good drainage keeps the building dry, prevents flooding and water-logging, and reduces dampness that causes disease and weakens structures.
summary.explanation: Dry, well-drained sites protect both the building and the health of animals.

summary.questionText: Give three ways of maintaining farm structures.
summary.correctAnswer: Repairing damaged roofs and walls, painting or treating timber against rot and termites, cleaning regularly, and replacing broken fence posts and gates.
summary.explanation: Regular repair, treatment and cleaning keep structures functional and prolong their life.

summary.questionText: Name three water structures and their uses on a farm.
summary.correctAnswer: A well supplies water, a tank stores water, and a trough provides drinking water for livestock.
summary.explanation: These structures collect, store and deliver water for crops and animals.

hoq.questionText: A dairy farmer in Kilimanjaro has only a small piece of land but wants to keep several improved dairy cows. Which housing system and siting decision is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Free-range grazing over a wide pasture far from the home
A zero-grazing unit sited downwind on well-drained ground near water and a road
Keeping the cows inside the family farmhouse for warmth
A poultry house converted into a milking parlour with no drainage

hoq.explanation: With limited land, a zero-grazing unit allows several cows to be kept in one place while feed is carried to them; siting it downwind, on well-drained ground near water and a road ensures hygiene, accessibility and good drainage.

hoq.questionText: A farmer's iron-sheet poultry house has many sick birds, foul smell and damp litter. Which combination of faults BEST explains this and how should it be corrected?

options.text: Too much ventilation and lighting; close all the openings permanently
Poor ventilation and a floor that is hard to clean; improve airflow and clean and dry the house regularly
The birds are simply too few; add many more birds to the same space
The house is too far from the road; move it closer to the road only

hoq.explanation: Foul smell, dampness and disease point to poor ventilation and a floor that is hard to clean; improving airflow and regular cleaning and drying remove ammonia and moisture and reduce disease.

hoq.questionText: A farmer must choose walling material for a grain store in a hot, termite-prone area but has a limited budget. Which choice BEST balances durability, pest protection and cost?

options.text: Untreated timber poles and mud only, because they are cheapest
Burnt bricks or cement blocks, which resist termites, rot and fire and last long despite higher cost
Grass thatch walls, because they keep the store cool
Thin polythene sheeting, because it is light and easy to fix

hoq.explanation: For a long-lasting grain store in a termite-prone area, burnt bricks or cement blocks resist termites, rot and fire and protect the grain better; though they cost more, they are the most durable and worthwhile choice.
